statement: A remediation written from an incident's narrative must be tested before it is documented. The #436 goal asked the contributor note to say 'build dist/ first', because the incident ran an unbuilt checkout. With dist/ built, npx @cejel/cejel@0.6.3 inside the checkout still ran the cejel on PATH: npx never links the root project's own bin. The unbuilt state was incidental, so the note would have taught a false fix. Rule: before documenting a workaround, reproduce the failure with the workaround applied.

An environment variable named for 'the package' can describe a different package than the one you mean. Under npx, npm_package_version is the working-directory project's version, not the requested or running one: in a 0.6.3 checkout, npx @cejel/cejel@0.6.2 correctly ran 0.6.2 while npm_package_version said 0.6.3, so treating it as the request would have warned falsely. The trap is told apart only by PATH order: npx-installed bins come first. Rule: test a candidate signal on the case where it would be wrong, not only where it is right.
